newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentines occupying Fiat plant fail to end row.
newsitem.headline: Argentines occupying Fiat plant fail to end row.

text.p: Talks between Italian carmaker Fiat SpA and some 700 workers occupying a Fiat motor and gearbox plant in Argentina's Cordoba province failed to solve the dispute on Monday.

"The conflict is continuing. The company is negotiating with the participation of the Labor Ministry of Cordoba province," Jorge Rendo, manager of institutional relations at Fiat Argentina, told Reuters.
Rendo said that, if the occupation continued, Fiat would start importing parts from plants in Brazil and Italy. So far, there are plenty of parts at the plant.
Workers from a car-part factory who were transferred to the Fiat Ferreyra car plant have been occupying the factory for five days demanding they keep the same pay and conditions.

The local chief of the car workers' union SMATA, Jose Campellone, said on Sunday that the occupation "is for an indefinite period" and unionsts would stage a major demonstration outside the plant on Thursday, when Argentine trade unions begin a nationwide 36-hour general strike.
